 LIVE Newcastle vs Arsenal - Premier League: Bruno Guimaraes STARTS on return to his former club as champions take on under-pressure Magpies
 By WILL PICKWORTH, SPORTS REPORTER 
 Updated: 12:30 EST, 21 November 2026 
 --> 
 --> 
 --> 
 Follow  Daily Mail Sport's live blog for the latest score, team news and updates as Manchester City   entertain Fulham  in the Premier League at the Etihad Stadium.  
 17:31 1 ' Newcastle 0-0 Arsenal
 The boos are already out.
 Bruno Guimaraes first touch is not only greeted with boos, but also with a chant that I can't repeat. It's rather fruity.
 I'm pretty sure it's the same one they sing for Alexander Isak when he comes here with Liverpool.
 Share 17:30 1 ' KICK-OFF: Newcastle 0-0 Arsenal
 Here we go then.
 This fixture has delivered plenty of crackers over the years, so lets hope it does so again tonight.
 There is a monster roar as the players take to their positions and this game gets underway.
 Let the fun commence.
 Share 17:29 'Yasir Al-Rumayyan in the stands'
 Craig Hope at St. James' Park: 
 Newcastle chairman Yasir Al-Rumayyan & co-owner Jamie Reuben in attendance here at SJP. Temperatures being taken, you feel... Share 17:28 Electric atmosphere
 No matter Newcastle's form, St. James' Park always delivers in big games. This place is bouncing.
 Hey Jude is blasted out as the players emerge from the tunnel, before some boos break out as they notice Bruno Guimaraes hop, skip and jump his way onto the pitch.
 You can already feel that this clash is going to have that extra bit of spice to usual.
 Sit back and prepare to be entertained.
 Share 17:26 Boos for Bruno
 There was much debate before this game over the reception Bruno Guimaraes would get returning to St. James' Park.
 Well, the answer has been emphatic.
 He was greeted with a whole host of boos as he entered the stadium earlier, and they only increased when he came out to warm up a half hour later.
 Now, those boos were when the ground was barely half full, so I imagine they will become deafening come his first touch in this game.
 He is seen in the same vein as Alexander Isak around these parts now.
 Share 17:23 'Jaissle makes a statement'
 Craig Hope at St. James' Park: 
 As ever, Newcastle supporters have been furiously debating the merit, or otherwise, of Jaissle's team selection. This time, it's as much about who isn't starting. Not only are summer signings Nico Gonzalez and Matias Fernandez-Pardo (combined £101m), there is no place at all in the squad for Baz Toure and Aladji Bamba (combined £72.5m). The omission of the quartet feels like quite a statement from the Newcastle manager, who wants greater control over transfers in January. That is, if he gets that far. Share 17:21 Arsenal Team News - Bruno G. STARTS
 Look who is back.
 William Saliba is back on the bench for Arsenal, with Ezri Konsa continuing in the centre of defence.
 Mikel Arteta's only change from the win over Hull sees Eberechi Eze come in on the left for Christos Tzolis.
 That means, of course, that Bruno Guimaraes stars against his old club.
 Share 17:19 Newcastle Team News - Miley STARTS
 Now that is what you call a young midfield.
 Matthias Jaissle has named a midfield pairing of two teenagers, Lewis Miley and Sean Steur. This is going to be one hell of a tough test for them.
 Will Osula continues to lead the line with Yoane Wissa warming the bench once again.
 No Joelinton involved this evening.
 Share 17:15 Over to Tyneside
 We are saving the best until last today.
 It's already been an afternoon full of entertainment, with shocks at both the Etihad and Stamford Bridge. Is there room for one more at St. James' Park?
 Well, a downbad Newcastle are about to take on high-flying table-toppers Arsenal, who can simply do no wrong right now. Anything other than a Gunners win would be a shock.
 Kick-off on Tyneside is just 15 minutes away, so strap in and get ready for a bumpy ride.
 This should be fun.
 Share 17:12 The bottom half
 Crystal Palace fans, look away.
 You may have a new manager, but it's the same old story. That defeat at Coventry sees the Eagles stay rock bottom.
 Meanwhile, Sunderland's point at Aston Villa sees them leap above Manchester United in the table...
 The Red Devils are 19th ahead of a trip to Anfield. Gulp.
 Share 17:10 The top half of the table
 Wow, just look at Bournemouth.
 They have flown up to fourth in the Premier League, while Chelsea are starting to drop like a stone.
 The table is much better-looking for Tottenham after their horrific start to the season; they have flown into the top half.
 Meanwhile, if their rivals Arsenal win at Newcastle tonight, they will go eight clear at the top.
